name: Light Grey Green
lede: Light Grey Green is a descriptive name for a pale, softly greyed spring green, and it has been in color charts since 1912.

sections.title: A name that says what it is
sections.body:
The name is a recipe: a [[green]], lightened and greyed. Ridgway's 1912 atlas shows it at plate VII, hue 37, tone d, and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates the name to 1912 [1]. The ISCC-NBS system covers it in block 135, and the xkcd color survey carries it too [1]. Ridgway, ISCC-NBS and Maerz and Paul also file a near-identical swatch, 1.9 units away, as Neuvider Green [1].

In the books the phrase is plain description. Birren quotes a person with colored hearing who saw the first half of the word *Tuesday* as a light gray-green and the end as yellow [2]. That is one person's synesthesia, not a standard color [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: On screen it is close to [[pistachio]] and [[light-grey-green]], a paler cousin of [[sage]] [1]. It is very rare in painting: only 2 of 23,781 paintings in our archive hold a color within six units of it over at least five per cent of the canvas, and one of them is [[painting:nga-72328|Roses]], dated 1890 [3]. Those are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so a match is not a pigment test [3].
